S1_consent_precedes_storage.how_verified: Read apps/bot/src/domain/inviteList.ts's resolvePersonalCodeIdentity/relinkToExistingAccount and apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts's makeStartHandler directly, not the design doc's account of them. Three sub-cases traced: (1) 'linked' branch -- the UPDATE at inviteList.ts:374-378 writes only tgId/tgUsername/lang onto the pre-created row, guarded `WHERE id = a.id AND tg_id IS NULL` inside a `for('update')`-locked transaction (race-safe: a second near-simultaneous tap affects zero rows and falls through to the documented re-check). Confirmed this is the identical write shape apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts's resolveOrCreateUser already performs unconditionally, before any consent check, on every ordinary /start (verified by reading user.ts:37-68 directly) -- this is pre-existing, previously-reviewed platform behavior (REQ-010/014), not a new S1 exposure introduced by this diff. No Profile write, no phone/email, on this path. (2) 'collision-relinked' branch -- relinkToExistingAccount only touches invite_list_entries (repoint/delete, both organizer-owned bookkeeping this requirement itself introduces) and invite_codes.issuedToUserId; never reads or writes profiles/registrations for either A or B; the AuditLog payload is {fromUserId, toUserId, eventId} -- no PII. Constructed the negative case: a caller who has never consented (consent_pd_at still null) taps a personal code that hits the collision branch -- traced that resolvePersonalCodeIdentity runs entirely before makeStartHandler's own consent-gate check (start.ts:615), and the relink writes nothing about B's own submitted data, so this ordering does not let unconsented self-disclosed data reach storage; the fields written are exactly the same minimal-identity category item (1) already establishes as out of S1's scope. (3) createNamedGuestUser (inviteList.ts:21-39) -- plain INSERT with tgId/tgUsername/lang all NULL, no Profile row, matching REQ-010's already-proven multi-NULL-tg_id shape; confirmed no phone/email/name is ever written to `users` by this function.

S2_authorization_checked_and_negative_pa.how_verified: Read all four handler entry points in apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteList.ts directly. Every one (makeInviteListAddHandler, makeInviteListHandler, makeInviteListIssueCallbackHandler, makeInviteListRemoveCallbackHandler, makeInviteListRemoveConfirmCallbackHandler) resolves the entry/event's own chapterId first (never trusts a chapterId the caller could supply) and then calls the identical, unchanged, previously-reviewed requireOrganizerForChapter(db, BigInt(tgId), event.chapterId) BEFORE any read of entry data beyond event resolution or any write. Read apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts's checkOrganizerForChapter predicate directly: role 'member' -> not-organizer refusal; role 'organizer' with chapterId !== targetChapterId -> wrong-chapter refusal; role 'owner' -> allowed for all chapters. Constructed the negative cases named in security-invariants.md: (a) a member (including an EventStaff-only account, which per S2's own definition is not a role value on users.role and therefore reads as 'member' here) tapping /invite_list_add, /invite_list, invite_list:issue:<id>, or invite_list:remove:<id> is refused on the handler itself, not merely absent from a menu -- confirmed by reading the refusal branch precedes every write/read call in each handler; (b) an organizer of chapter A given a valid entryId belonging to chapter B's event: getEventIdForInviteListEntry/getInviteListEntryById re-derive the entry's real owning event, getEventById resolves its real chapterId, and requireOrganizerForChapter is evaluated against THAT chapterId (never a client-supplied one) -- so the wrong-chapter refusal fires correctly even when the entryId itself is valid. The two-step remove flow (invite_list:remove:<id> then invite_list:remove:confirm:<id>) re-checks S2 independently on BOTH steps (read directly at inviteList.ts:275 and :320), closing the TOCTOU gap named in S2's own guidance (a role check present on the first tap but absent on the action that performs it).

S13_deletion_anonymizes_preserves_aggreg.how_verified: Per this role's mandatory migration duty: read apps/bot/drizzle/0008_optimal_medusa.sql directly (not the schema doc's description of it). It is a pure additive migration -- one CREATE TABLE invite_list_entries, four ADD CONSTRAINT (all ON DELETE RESTRICT, matching the schema's uniform posture), one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX -- zero ALTER, DROP, or RENAME of any existing table/column. No column holding personal data or attendance history is dropped, renamed, or rewritten by this migration, so the S13 sign-off duty (drops/renames/rewrites of PII or attendance columns) is not triggered by the migration itself. Separately verified the application-level hard-DELETE remove mechanism (removeInviteListEntry) cannot retroactively alter a past event's published attendance figures: invite_list_entries is a membership/outreach-status table that is never the source of any registered/attended/seats-taken figure (those derive from `registrations`/`checked_in_at`, both entirely untouched by any write in this diff) -- deleting a list entry removes only the organizer's own list membership row, never a registration or check-in fact, so no aggregate can silently change as a result.
